tests.name: New user can sign up and lands on a funded dashboard
tests.summary:
Completed the requested account details for Kane Tester, using kanew6m5k1@mlyfo.app and the username kanew6m5k1.
Confirmed that @kanew6m5k1 was available, entered the requested password, and created the account.
The new account opened with the heading “Welcome, Kane” and a wallet balance of $500.00.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved contact's address
tests.summary:
You asked to sign in and check the supplied wallet address using the Shield page.
The Shield page was opened, the address was entered, and the address check was run.
The result marked the address as “Blocked” and indicated that it resembles Ada’s saved address but is not the same address.

Entered the provided wallet address and checked it.
The result marked the address as “Blocked” and said it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not.

tests.name: A payment over the spend limit waits for password confirmation
tests.summary:
You asked to send $150 to @ada for rent.
Entered “pay @ada 150 for rent” in the message field and selected the $150 payment option.
Reviewed the confirmation showing $150.00 to @ada and the per-payment limit, then entered the provided password and confirmed the payment.
The payment was completed, and the page confirmed: “Sent $150.00 to @ada.”

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
Checked the requested link, https://phantorn-airdrop.app/claim, using the Quick check option.
The scan marked the link as Dangerous.
The listed reason stated that the address imitates Phantom.

tests.name: Shield refuses to save a look-alike of a saved person
tests.summary:
You asked to add a person named “Ada new” with the provided wallet address.
Entered the name and wallet address, then selected “Save person.”
The page reported that the address was not saved because it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not.
“Ada new” was not added to the people list.

tests.name: Paying a name that is both a saved person and another user asks who you meant
tests.summary:
You asked to send $5.00 to Semi for coffee.
Entered “pay semi 5 for coffee” and selected the $5.00 payment option.
The page asked which Semi you meant and showed both your contact Semi and the Mlyfo user @semi.
Selected your contact Semi.
The payment was confirmed as sent: $5.00 to Semi.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved Ethereum and Base address
tests.summary:
Opened the sign-in option, then went to the Shield address-check page for the requested wallet address.
The address field contained 0x7a3f9cE5b801Dd3fA7426C9e0B1f8a5d3e27c4b9.
The check marked the address as “Blocked,” said it resembles Ada (Base)’s saved address but is not the same address, and labelled it for Ethereum and Base.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved Ethereum and Base address
tests.summary:
The automation misread a result badge that visibly contains both “Ethereum” and “Base.” The result itself also correctly showed the blocked warning and the Ada (Base) look-alike message.
Update the verification to read the combined network badge as containing both labels, rather than expecting a different label structure.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
tests.summary:
Opened the requested Mlyfo manifest page.
Confirmed the page presents the “Mlyfo on your Android phone” heading, a “Download the keyboard” button, and Chrome installation guidance.
Confirmed the keyboard privacy information states that internet is its only permission and keystrokes never leave the phone.
Confirmed the “Check your download” section includes a SHA-256 fingerprint.
The displayed manifest shows the app name “Mlyfo” with display mode “standalone”.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
tests.summary:
Opened the Mlyfo web app manifest at the requested address.
Confirmed the manifest identifies the app as “Mlyfo” and uses the standalone display mode.
The Mlyfo page information also showed Android installation guidance, a “Download the keyboard” button, privacy statements that internet is its only permission and keystrokes stay on the phone, and a SHA-256 download fingerprint.
